summary: Empty trade list, judged on reasoning and the information available. Standing aside was defensible: cash was only about $7 above the 10% buffer, the Proposer made no proposals, and I can't invent trades. I gave size and the CARG/NFP event cluster as the reasons, not a blanket idle-cash rule (L4 narrow reading held). The IDXX re-anchor to $630 was routed through thesis_updates and is stored in close.json, as L1/L5 ask. The weak point is stale marks, the third day running. The held-position review used intraday or earlier prices, and the book then fell sharply into the close (equity $622.50 vs the $636.18 I cited, day P&L -$11.02, drawdown 2.15%; VOO -4.6%, VTI -4.3%, BTC -5.7%, MSM -4.4%, IDXX -4.0%, SPY proxy -4.4%). Recomputed from close.json: BTC/USD is about $75.9k (13.30 / 0.000175228 sh) against the roughly $75.3k stop, so 0.8% away and not 5% as I wrote from a $79.3k mark. It is the nearest stop in the book and a close-basis trip is one bad session away. MSM is about $110.95 against a stop of about $108 (9% under the $118.72 fill), 2.6% away, where I called it 'well clear'. IDXX is about $670.7 against the new $630 stop (6% away, not 10%): the re-anchor was set against a $700 mark that did not hold at the close. VOO/VTI invalidate on SPY closing below its 200-day average (about 727); if the $766.81 SPY level in the market note was the 11-04 close, a 4.4% drop leaves it only about 0.8% above that line. That is an inference, since the note's SPY level is not dated. VTI is about 4% above its -8% fill stop. No clause has tripped on close-basis data: BTC is -9.3% on cost vs a 10% stop; no exchange failure or adverse regulatory action appears in the notes; CARG's print is after the close and unread. The hold-through-CARG call is the one real exposure: at the close CARG is 5.7% of equity at about $37.17, so a 15-20% gap costs roughly $5.3-7.1 (about 0.9-1.1% of equity). That is a bit above the $5-7 I wrote and the 11-06 open is the test. Market stance 'neutral' was reasonable on the evidence available but looks stale after a -4.4% SPY day; tomorrow's agents should re-read it against the 200-day line and the NFP outcome.
lessons: L5 recurs: reasoning cited pre-close marks (BTC about $79.3k, IDXX about $700.6, CARG about $37.00) while close.json shows lower prices on a -4% day. Before writing stop distances, take the latest mark in inputs/portfolio.json and say which mark it is; where the day is volatile, add a line saying the distances may be stale by the close.

A stop re-anchored to a mark the same day (IDXX $630 vs about $700) can end up near the market within a session when the name has just run 20%+. When re-anchoring after a large gain, state the distance on a mark 4-5% lower, not only on the current mark.

Name the BTC/USD price stop (about $75.3k) and the SPY 200-day line (about 727) as live thresholds for 11-06, both under 1% away on close-basis numbers, together with the dated catalysts: CARG reaction and NFP on 11-06, MSCI crypto-treasury decision on 11-11.

Staying in cash was reasoned correctly, but the book's cash share rose to about 11.4% after the sell-off. If a clean buy fits tomorrow, pair it with a candidate that the Proposer has fully sized (the VNQ/EXEL request has now gone unanswered four runs). Do not buy on the dip without checking the 200-day line first.
